source_text: Lege et de hoc quartum operis mei librum: et quantum diabolo, quem patrem tuum dicis, ac libidini matri tuae, sub criminandi specie blandiaris, intelleges.
pass_a_gloss: Read also about this the fourth book of my work: and you will understand how much, under the appearance of accusing, you flatter the devil, whom you call your father, and lust your mother.

lemmas.lexica: LS libido; Blaise not a nature-sin substance

pass_b_english: Read the fourth book of my work on this subject too. You will understand how much, under the guise of accusation, you flatter the devil whom you call your father, and lust, your mother.

choices.why: Julian refuses to make marital desire a nature-sin substance planted by the devil.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
